svg.aria-label: Four verses from Katha, each in Sanskrit, transliteration and English

g.text: “Thy business is with the action only, never with its fruits; so let not the fruit of
action be thy motive, nor be thou to inaction attached.”
RAMAYANA · BALA KANDA 2.14 · THE FIRST SHLOKA
मा निषाद प्रतिष्ठां त्वमगमः शाश्वतीः समाः
mā niṣāda pratiṣṭhāṁ tvamagamaḥ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ
“O fowler, since you have slain one of a pair of Krauñcas, you shall never attain
यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत।
yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata
“Whenever there is decay of righteousness, O Bhârata, and there is exaltation of
unrighteousness, then I Myself come forth;”
“Having saluted the Supreme Deity (Narayana) and the highest of all male beings
(Nara) and also the Goddess of Learning (Sarasvati), let us cry success!”
